Day 12 of 100 · AWS Networking Foundations

VPC Peering

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityAWS Networking FoundationsTopic verified by artifact

VPC Peering connects two VPCs directly, but routing, addressing and security rules still decide whether applications can communicate.

Architecture / mental model

VPC A route table ↔ peering connection ↔ VPC B route table

How it works

A peering connection creates a private routing relationship between two VPCs. Both sides need routes for the peer CIDR, and the application path still passes through Security Group and network controls.

Peering is not transitive. If VPC A peers with B and B peers with C, A does not automatically gain a route through B to C.

Overlapping CIDR ranges prevent the clean routing model peering depends on, so address planning made early can determine whether later connectivity is simple or painful.

Hands-on reference

aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections
aws ec2 describe-route-tables

Verification

Confirm the peering state is active, routes exist on both sides, Security Groups permit the application flow, then test the actual service port rather than stopping at ICMP.

Field note / gotcha

A healthy peering object does not create routes for you. 'Peering active' and 'traffic routable' are separate facts.

Security considerations

Route only CIDRs that need connectivity and keep service-level access scoped with Security Groups rather than treating the peer VPC as automatically trusted.

What I learned

Connectivity is a chain: relationship, routes, policy and application listener all have to agree.
